newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israel's PM says ready to discuss settlements.
newsitem.headline: Israel's PM says ready to discuss settlements.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that he was willing to discuss the fate of Jewish settlements in occupied areas in peace talks with the Palestinians.

"We can and we will discuss our differences, including on the issues of settlements, around the negotiating table...and hopefully come to a final settlement and end once and for all the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians," Netanyahu told a joint news conference with Jordan's King Hussein.
Netanyahu made the statement after meeting King Hussein for summit talks on the crisis in Israeli-Palestinian ties since a double suicide bombing in a Jerusalem market last month.
Israel blames Moslem militants for the attack and has accused Palestinian President Yasser Arafat of failing to crack down on militants operating from self-rule areas.

Peace talks between the parties had already been deadlocked since March when Israel broke ground on a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. The fate of settlements on land occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war is one of the most contentious issues in any final peace deal.

Netanyahu said he had information that militants were planning more attacks in Israel. He announced no easing of an Israeli security clampdown on Palestinian areas since the July 30 blasts, which killed 14 people as well as the bombers.
